title: The colimit description of invertible orders
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a
torsion sheaf on the etale site
of a $K$-scheme; write $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$ and let $I_K$ be the
set of integers invertible in $K$, as in
[def-kun-torsion-invertible]. Then $F$ has orders invertible in
$K$ if and only if

$$
F=\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n].
$$

The colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is taken in the category of etale abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], over the positive integers in $I_K$ ordered by divisibility, with inclusion maps $F[n]\hookrightarrow F[m]$ for $n\mid m$. The kernels are those of [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]. The displayed equality means that the canonical map $c:\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n]\to F$ induced by the inclusions is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The full subcategory of positive integers whose cast to K is nonzero is filtered: 1 is an object, and the product of two objects is a common divisibility upper bound; parallel arrows are unique. The diagram of kernel sheaves and its cocone of kernel inclusions are the explicit definitions in the item module, and the colimit descent is the prescribed comparison.

For any additive functor E preserving finite limits and colimits of the relevant size, the comparison after applying E is monic because every colimit representative comes from a kernel object and each kernel inclusion is monic. It is epic exactly when every element of E.obj F is killed by an allowed positive integer: one direction represents a preimage by a kernel object; the other lifts a killed element through the preserved kernel and then through a colimit coprojection. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism exactly under the stalkwise annihilator condition.

source.place: kernel union argument, made categorical in the proof helper

proof.text: Apply the preceding criterion to each geometric stalk, using the Mathlib finite-limit preservation instance (the left-exact clause of [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]) and the Mathlib skyscraper right adjoint to obtain colimit preservation directly for AddCommGrpCat. The stalk is the Mathlib sheafFiber realization of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Transport the criterion along uliftSheafFiberIso and use [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to reflect isomorphisms. The definition [def-kun-torsion-invertible] is exactly the required annihilator condition, so both implications follow.

proof_origin.place: Kernel-colimit and geometric-stalk argument of the blueprint, implemented using Mathlib concrete filtered-colimit representatives, preservation of kernels, the skyscraper adjunction, and the existing geometric-stalk conservative family.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported single stalk argument into five steps: the small filtered invertible-integer diagram and canonical map, exact identification of each kernel stalk, an explicit elementary proof that the directed subgroup union is the colimit, preservation of that comparison by stalks, and conservativity in both directions. Clarified the canonical interpretation of the displayed equality without changing the assertion or hypotheses. Added kernel and colimit notion dependencies; removed the unnecessary use of the unrestricted torsion-union theorem. Exactness of stalks was missing from the imported citation list and is now cited. All required lemmas already exist; no new nodes. Mathlib searches ran through msearch.py; LeanSearch was unavailable. No exact project attachment was found.
